headline: Committee discusses shoreline erosion impacts on coastal properties; chair proposes deferral

meeting.body: Maui County Council Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee
meeting.summary: The committee's only agenda item was shoreline erosion, with presentations and public testimony. The chair said the item would be deferred if there were no objections; no member response is recorded in the facts.
meeting.recap: The committee's only agenda item was shoreline erosion impacts on coastal properties.[[0:06:07]] She said newer sea level mapping is not yet available for Maui, partly because federal funding fell through.[[0:42:43]] She said the Maui Planning Commission made the erosion hazard line the shoreline setback line.[[0:50:40]] One testifier asked whether the County should encourage local families to put their life savings into coastal hazard areas.[[1:02:39]] The dean said building the same sea level tools for Maui would take two to three years at about a million dollars a year.[[1:39:19]] He said five to 13 tropical cyclones are projected near Hawaiʻi with El Niño conditions this year.[[1:40:43]] A planning official said some Lahaina shoreline rebuilds must file hold harmless agreements (agreements that release others from liability).[[2:26:13]] The chair said the item would be deferred (set aside for now) if there were no objections.[[2:30:26]]
meeting.next: The coastal scientist said her working group is preparing a grant proposal to the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation for a stormwater area in North Kīhei.

moments.q: "El Nino years are characterized by weather on steroids."
